correctness.rationale: The solid is explicitly defined by a 24-vertex, 36-edge rational polyhedron. Crossing-edge counting is exact for all nonexceptional central planes. The only three chamber walls are found by testing vertex dot-products, giving an exhaustive five-cell partition with types 8,10,6,8,6. The ten-gon cell is a specified spherical triangle whose elementary exact solid angle is calculated independently by two methods. A universal edge-sign probability based on endpoint angle arccos(4/5) gives the exact first moment; support and normalization fix the other probabilities. The actual packaged Python program passed exact enumeration, algebraic/numerical identities and a Haar consistency simulation. No finite experiment is used as proof of continuous orientation coverage.

originality.rationale: Targeted comparisons found no previously stated exact Haar central-section law for the regular truncated octahedron. The closest full primary text, arXiv:2304.14239v1, catalogs general slicing chambers and affine extremizers of the identical 3D permutahedron but does not give central-orientation probabilities; its claims do not imply the displayed numerical or elementary exact Haar law without additional integration. Published findings for neighboring solids concern different vertex directions. The inaccessible full 2005 periodic-surface paper and older stereology tables remain residual priority risks, not contrary coverage.

value.rationale: A natural Archimedean space-filling convex polyhedron and the 3-permutahedron have a previously unextracted complete central-section type probability law. Computing all three exact probabilities, particularly the decagonal solid-angle mass, is a motivated finite classification with stereological significance and is not subsumed by the mere catalog of possible affine sections. The exact mean serves as an independent structural check rather than the sole contribution.
